title: Canonical biduality of a finite module into a bounded injective complex
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $L\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use derived internal Hom on the one-object ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Suppose that $L$ is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and that the scalar-action morphism $h:A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,L)$ is an isomorphism. Then the canonical biduality morphism
$$\delta_{M,L}:M[0]\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],L),L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(A)$. Here $\delta_{M,L}$ is the transpose of evaluation $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M[0],L)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0]\to L$ under the derived tensor--Hom adjunction; equivalently, on compatible Hom representatives it sends $m$ to evaluation $\varphi\mapsto\varphi(m)$. The assertion concerns this canonical morphism, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target. No projectivity of $M$, localness or completeness of $A$, or finite generation of the cohomology of $L$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, canonical double-dual evaluation in its proof, specialized to a finite module; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A69, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism-technical, and Tag 066E, lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent, clause (2). The argument only uses bounded injectives and the scalar-action isomorphism for L.

proof.text: Put $K=M[0]$. Its only possibly nonzero cohomology is $H^0(K)=M$; all its cohomology modules are therefore finite, and they vanish above degree zero. The Noetherian cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] makes $K$ pseudo-coherent. Choose a bounded injective representative $I$ of $L$ as in the hypothesis. If $I^j=0$ for $j<a$, then $H^j(L)=H^j(I)=0$ for $j<a$. Thus $L\in D^+(A)$ in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories].

source.place: Tag 066E, lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent, clause (2); bounded representative and the hypotheses of Tag 0A68 (2)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-pseudocoherent] with its $(R,K,L,M)$ equal to $(A,M[0],L,L)$. Step 1 verifies pseudo-coherence and the bounded-below hypothesis; its last hypothesis is exactly the given bounded injective representative of $L$. Consequently, writing $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,L)$ and $B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$, the specified evaluation comparison $e:T\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,L)$ is an isomorphism. This uses neither projectivity of $M$ nor finiteness of the cohomology of $L$.

source.place: Tag 0A68, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism, case (2), the pseudo-coherent case underlying Tag 0A69

proof.text: On the small one-object ringed site with trivial topology, [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] supplies the derived tensor bifunctor, its unit $A[0]$, and the unitor $\lambda_K:A[0]\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Define $b=e\circ(h\otimes1_K)\circ\lambda_K^{-1}$. Since $h$ is invertible, $h^{-1}\otimes1_K$ is inverse to $h\otimes1_K$ by bifunctoriality. Thus $b$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $\lambda_K\circ(h^{-1}\otimes1_K)\circ e^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, displayed composite in the proof

proof.text: It remains to identify this particular $b$. Write $\epsilon_{X,Y}:R\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,Y)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}X\to Y$ for evaluation. By the specified transpose of [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], uncurrying $b$ with $B$ on the left gives, after inserting the canonical associators, unitors and symmetry, the morphism $\epsilon_{L,L}\circ(h\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\circ\lambda_{B\otimes K}^{-1}:B\otimes K\to L$. The scalar-action morphism $h$ is adjoint to the unit action, so $\epsilon_{L,L}\circ(h\otimes1_L)=\lambda_L$. Hence this uncurrying equals $\lambda_L\circ(1_{A[0]}\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\circ\lambda_{B\otimes K}^{-1}=\epsilon_{K,L}$ by naturality of the unitor. The natural adjunction bijection and symmetry in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] are injective on morphisms, so $b$ is exactly the transpose of $\epsilon_{K,L}$, namely $\delta_{M,L}$. Step 3 therefore proves that the canonical biduality morphism is an isomorphism.

The delivery creates no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. In clones/live and clones/side-live the item is still unsplit, so it has not been superseded, and it is not a 2026-10-21 re-split. No SGA citations. Step 1: by 066E(2), M[0] is pseudo-coherent, and L is in D+ because its bounded injective representative has a lower bound. Step 2: lem-trf-derived-evaluation-pseudocoherent (0A68(2)) applied with (R,K,L,M)=(A,M[0],L,L); all its hypotheses are discharged. Step 3: b=e∘(h⊗1)∘λ^{-1} is invertible; I checked the explicit inverse. Step 4: I recomputed that b uncurries to ε_{L,L}(h⊗ε_{K,L})λ^{-1}=ε_{K,L}, using h = transpose of λ_L, naturality of the unitor, and the counit description in lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal. So b=δ, and the canonical-map clause is proved. The bookkeeping of associators and symmetry is compressed but routine. Small cases check out: Z with Z/n into Z (Z/n → Z/n[-1] → Z/n), a field with L=k[3], A=k[x]/x^2 with L=A, and M=0. Dropping finite cohomology of L is correct, since the 0A68/0A69 argument never uses it. A DFS over the snapshot finds no cycle.
